summary.title: Lambda architecture - Wikipedia
summary.one_liner: Lambda architecture combines batch processing for accurate, complete views with stream processing for low-latency views, merged in a serving layer.
keywords: how to combine batch and real-time data
takeaways: Lambda architecture has three layers: a batch layer for accurate recomputed views, a speed layer for low-latency views of recent data, and a serving layer that answers queries.
The batch layer recomputes from the complete immutable data set and replaces precomputed views, which lets it fix errors.
The speed layer trades accuracy and completeness for latency and is later replaced by batch results once they are available.
Criticism centers on the complexity of maintaining two code bases that must produce the same results; Kappa architecture proposes a pure streaming alternative.
summary.summary: The Wikipedia article describes lambda architecture, a data-processing design for massive data volumes that uses batch processing for comprehensive, accurate views and stream processing for real-time views, with a serving layer that combines them for queries. It explains the role of each layer and lists typical technologies, such as Hadoop for batch and Kafka, Storm, Spark, or Flink for streaming, and Druid or Cassandra for serving. It also covers the append-only, immutable data model, optimization techniques, real-world uses at Metamarkets, Yahoo, and Netflix, and criticism leading to the Kappa architecture alternative.
